ranked.headline: Pretrained protein and chemical embeddings fused with structure, dynamics and energetics for variant and site ranking
ranked.summary: New benchmarks with wet-lab validation, plus physics- and dynamics-conditioned predictors, are reshaping how enzymes, mutants and ligand sites get ranked.

ranked.headline: Generative design conditions on pharmacophores, pockets and objectives, with ADME-aware re-scoring
ranked.summary: Pocket-, pharmacophore- and objective-conditioned generators now pair with exposure-, toxicity- and pose-ranking evaluators that reorder which designs survive.

ranked.headline: Histology anchors 3D reconstruction and gene-panel prediction in spatial transcriptomics
ranked.summary: New methods use H&E morphology to reconstruct continuous 3D expression, predict 1,000-gene panels and statistically dissect histology–expression links.

ranked.headline: Generative models disentangle cell state from treatment to predict unseen perturbations
ranked.summary: New preprints pair full-gene, graph-guided and disentangled generative perturbation predictors with simulators and benchmarks for evaluating single-cell methods.

ranked.headline: Omics databases move to cell-, CpG- and niche-level resolution with built-in analysis tools
ranked.summary: NAR database updates and cohort atlases arrive together, mapping GWAS, methylation, spatial and kinase data onto finer cellular and molecular contexts.

ranked.headline: Datasets, ensembles and pose metrics for structure-based ligand modeling across ligand classes
ranked.summary: New datasets, ensemble generators and pose-quality metrics address input diversity and evaluation for ML-driven structure-based ligand modeling.

ranked.headline: Structure-linked annotation databases expand content and add machine-actionable, AI-ready access
ranked.summary: Six database updates pair expanded structural annotation with versioned APIs and MCP access, making these resources easier to query programmatically.

ranked.headline: Transcriptomic partitions and predictions get explicit null models and reproducibility audits
ranked.summary: New tests give spatial domains and scRNA-seq clusters formal significance, while audits expose limits in AlphaGenome, drug-response data and CRISPRi rankings.

ranked.headline: Ensemble generation and rare-event analysis replace single poses in biomolecular modeling
ranked.summary: New preprints extend ensemble generation to complexes and RNA, while benchmarks expose cofolding limits and ligand strain gets neural-potential estimates.

ranked.headline: Sequence, prior-knowledge and perturbation models are tested for what they actually capture
ranked.summary: Seven new items probe what protein language models, foundation embeddings and prior-informed predictors capture, and where dataset properties limit performance.

ranked.headline: Isoform and polyadenylation-site resolution extends to single-cell, long-read and proteomic readouts
ranked.summary: New APA tools, a long-read polyadenylation atlas and an aging isoform atlas tie transcript-level resolution to single-cell, structural and protein-level interpretation.

ranked.headline: Count-based, uncertainty-aware and sequence models link genetic variants to cell-type-specific expression
ranked.summary: New sc-eQTL, TWAS, and variant-scoring methods match genetic-effect models to donor and cell-type structure in expression and chromatin data.

ranked.headline: Designed antibodies and binders are being tested across variants, developability limits and function
ranked.summary: Four reports extend computational binder design to multi-variant targets, agentic workflows and failure-mode diagnosis beyond predicted affinity.

ranked.headline: Genome mining pairs learned and factorized models with large mobile-element and pathogen resources
ranked.summary: New work couples model-based gene discovery with shared databases and reproducible workflows for mobile elements, prophages, and pathogen genomics.

ranked.headline: Cross-genome alignments and orthology define repeats, coding sequence and complexes without reference annotation
ranked.summary: New tools and resources catalog tandem repeats, coding alignments and orthogroups across genomes, as near-complete assemblies of P. falciparum become available.

ranked.headline: Multi-species databases map circRNA translation, RBP sites and snoRNAs across vertebrate models
ranked.summary: Four November 2026 reports extend cross-species RNA annotation, from translatable circRNAs to RBP sites and snoRNAs, alongside a bat genome with lncRNA analysis.

ranked.headline: Predicted structures are judged by membrane geometry, ensembles, energetics and loop flexibility
ranked.summary: New work tests AlphaFold outputs against membrane geometry and beta-sheet polymorphism, while a GPU frustratometer makes energetic analysis feasible proteome-wide.

ranked.headline: Pretrained sequence and ontology embeddings are being adapted and benchmarked for downstream biological tasks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints benchmark and adapt pretrained embeddings across viral, microbial, gene and cell-level tasks, testing how well representations transfer.

ranked.headline: LLM pipelines extract structured toxicological evidence from full-text literature at corpus scale
ranked.summary: Three preprints apply LLMs to toxicology literature, from AOP evidence mapping to a continuously updated hepatotoxicity knowledge base.

ranked.headline: Alignment-free and sketch-based methods cut the cost of viral and sequence-level inference
ranked.summary: Four new tools replace full alignment or exhaustive comparison with read-, seed- or sketch-level inference, with reported speedups and laptop-scale deployment.

ranked.headline: Curated peptide databases paired with ML models for antimicrobial and ADMET prediction
ranked.summary: Leakage and inconsistent evaluation in peptide prediction tools motivate a standardized framework for comparing performance claims.

ranked.headline: Circuit models link spiking dynamics, recovery trajectories, and adversarial robustness
ranked.summary: Recent preprints connect spike-level mechanisms, multiscale V1 recovery, and connectome-constrained fly models to network-level dynamics.

ranked.headline: Outcome encodings and regulatory maps sharpen trait associations in non-human genomes
ranked.summary: Survival-based outcome encoding and large regulatory atlases are making genetic association findings in non-human models more testable.

ranked.headline: Graph models couple network topology with local features in biological prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply graph neural networks and hypergraph models to protein, gene regulatory, drug synergy, and single-cell problems.

ranked.headline: Computational models test neural and behavioral dynamics against quantitative data
ranked.summary: Recent work tests explicit neural and behavioral models against data, emphasizing biologically grounded inputs, memory structure, and feedback.

ranked.headline: Pretrained generative models repurposed for protein, DNA and molecular design tasks
ranked.summary: Three recent preprints reuse pretrained generative backbones across protein complexes, molecular inference and phage genome modeling.

ranked.headline: Single-cell multiomics link chromatin state and cell identity across basal ganglia
ranked.summary: Six published atlases now pair single-cell regulatory profiling with cross-species and population-level comparison in basal ganglia and striatum.

ranked.headline: Established genomic analysis steps re-engineered for speed and automation
ranked.summary: Recent deepTools4 and CLIPittyClip releases report benchmarked speed-ups and single-command workflows for established genomic analysis steps.

ranked.headline: Remote similarity and structural alignment extend protein function assignment
ranked.summary: Remote sequence and structural comparisons now assign function to proteins beyond Pfam and ECOD coverage.

ranked.headline: Protein and DNA language models applied to design, epitope prediction and data pruning
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one published study test how data pruning, sampling strategy, and structural context affect sequence model performance.

ranked.headline: Isoform-resolved atlases and regulatory networks expand plant gene regulation resources
ranked.summary: Population-scale isoform quantification is now linked to trait mapping, while curated plant regulatory networks extend to 240 species.

ranked.headline: Harmonized metadata and automated pipelines make public sequence archives reusable
ranked.summary: Public omics archives remain hard to reuse without harmonized metadata, automated reprocessing, and current NCBI submission and access tooling.

ranked.headline: Explicit inference of recombination hotspots and reticulate history in genomes
ranked.summary: Simulation-based and likelihood methods now estimate gene-level rates and reticulate lineage structure directly rather than absorbing them as noise.

ranked.headline: Compressed indexes now support k-mer updates, faster dictionaries, and genome matching
ranked.summary: Terabase pangenome assemblies demand indexes that query and update in compressed space rather than from raw sequence.

ranked.headline: Compact biomolecular models gain from input representation and targeted readouts
ranked.summary: Global correlation metrics overstate perturbation-response accuracy, prompting tighter evaluation and readout design across biomolecular models.

ranked.headline: Polymer models link chromatin structure, dynamics and looping mechanisms
ranked.summary: Polymer simulations now infer chromatin dynamics from Hi-C and test how well microscopy readouts constrain looping.

ranked.headline: Cytoskeletal mechanics and turnover set force networks in computational cell models
ranked.summary: Computational preprints now tie actin turnover, filament mechanics and cell deformability to how force is distributed within and between cells.

ranked.headline: Confidence scores and public benchmarks fail to certify sequence design outcomes
ranked.summary: Predicted confidence scores and public benchmarks are being audited for whether they can certify outcomes of generated biological designs.

ranked.headline: Stricter held-out protocols test generalization in molecular property prediction
ranked.summary: Recent items pair leakage-aware evaluation protocols with architectures for scaffold heterogeneity and conflicting evidence in drug and molecular modeling.

ranked.headline: Proteomics searches expand to proteoforms and dark proteome, with coverage gaps measured
ranked.summary: Foundation models, multi-enzyme DIA and rule-based peptide prioritization now extend assignable proteome space while exposing coverage biases.
